tests.description: The scripttest brain offers read, bash, edit, and write, then runAgency and agencyScript, then the caller's tools.
The system prompt has the primer, which names runAgency and agencyScript, and keeps the minimal brain's coding rules; the writer's tutorial is not on the main thread.
runAgency returns a program's type errors, one per line with its position counted from 1, and never raises std::run.
tests.expectedOutput: "The program was not run, because it has type errors:\nline 3, column 7: AG2002: Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'boolean' (condition)."

tests.description: runAgency runs a program with no type errors and returns what main returned.
agencyScript runs the program the writer returns, and returns what main returned with the program's source.
When the program cannot run, here because std::run is rejected, the failure includes the program's source.
When every draft is broken, the writer's failure comes back and std::run is never raised.
Starting the program raises std::run, and the program's own read raises std::read to the same handler.
